titel: Aromas dissolve in fat, water or alcohol
kurz: Many aroma compounds dissolve better in fat than in water. That is why fat carries flavour and spices open up more in oil.
bild_im_kopf: Like guests who only get home in the right taxi: some aromas only climb into fat, others only into water.
was_passiert: Aroma compounds are tiny, often volatile molecules. Many of them love fat: they dissolve well in oil or butter and linger longer in the mouth. Others dissolve in water or in alcohol. Heat makes aromas volatile, so warm food smells stronger, and long cooking drives scent compounds away.
warum_wichtig: Explains why low-fat versions taste flatter, why you toast spices in oil and why wine in a sauce dissolves different aromas than water.
faustregeln: Toast dry spices briefly in fat rather than sprinkling them into water.
Add fresh herbs only at the end; their scent compounds fly off.
A splash of wine or spirits dissolves aromas that water cannot reach.

stellschrauben.wirkung: more fat → more aroma stays in the mouth

praxis.text: A knob of cold butter at the end does not only thicken, it also carries the aromas.
